newsitem.title: USA: Notorious Florida child killer slain in prison.
newsitem.headline: Notorious Florida child killer slain in prison.

text.p: A convicted killer who committed one of Florida's most notorious child abuse murders was beaten to death in prison and police were investigating a possible link to a radio broadcast about the case, authorities said Wednesday.

Donald McDougall was serving a 34-year sentence for the sadistic 1982 slaying of 5-year-old Ursula Assaid, a case that attracted national attention because neighbours and school officials seemingly ignored evidence of child abuse in the weeks leading up to the girl's death.

About 200 inmates were present in the recreation compound at the Avon Park Correctional Institution when McDougall was fatally beaten Tuesday night with a piece of steel bar used by inmates as a horseshoe stake, said Sonya Dodds, spokeswoman for the Polk County Sheriff's Office.

Dodds said investigators were looking into allegations from witnesses to the killing that a radio broadcast about the Assaid case last week on Orlando FM radio station WTKS might have been a contributing factor in McDougall's slaying.
Arba Earl Barr, 33, an inmate serving 114 years for robbery and aggravated battery, was charged with first-degree murder in McDougall's death, she said.
"There is the indication that the broadcast done last week was a contributing, inciting factor to the beating and ultimately to the death of McDougall," she said.

Dodds said investigators had asked the station for a tape of the broadcast but could not confirm reports it contained suggestions that other inmates beat McDougall. The station's programme director was not immediately available for comment.
"We don't know what was on the broadcast other that what the witnesses said," Dodds said. "For whatever reason, Barr took it upon himself to become the avenger in this case."
McDougall had been put in protective custody at the prison last week following the broadcast but was returned to the general population at his own request.

McDougall and Ursula's mother, Susan Assaid of Altamonte Springs, were accused of torturing the child for 55 hours straight before her heart gave out. A book titled "No One Heard" was written about the case.

Authorities said Ursula was dunked in a sink full of ice water and forced to stand outside for hours without moving, in view of neighbours. Her body, found in a pond where McDougall had dumped it, was covered with welts, cuts and bruises.

The criminal investigation documented that at least 89 people knew Ursula was being abused and did not report it. School officials followed without question the mother's note instructing them not to give her any fluids even after the child collapsed on the school playground.
Susan Assaid pleaded guilty to manslaughter and testified against McDougall, who was convicted of second-degree murder.
Florida law was changed in the wake of Ursula's death, making child-abuse murders a capital crime punishable by the death penalty even when the killing is not premeditated.

In 1993 McDougall was scheduled to be released from prison due to overcrowding. But public protests led Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth's office to review the case and McDougall was kept behind bars.
